records.title: LT2 Engine Valve Lifter Tick and DFM Concerns
records.description: The C8 Corvette uses the LT2 6.2L V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management (DFM) which can deactivate any combination of cylinders. While the LT2 is generally reliable, some owners report lifter tick similar to the AFM issues on truck engines. The DFM system uses the same collapsible lifter technology. GM has released updated VLOM and lifter designs for the LT2. The tick is most noticeable on cold starts and usually disappears when warm. Severe cases may require lifter replacement.
records.solution: Mild cold-start tick is considered normal on LT2 by many in the Corvette community. Persistent tick that does not go away when warm warrants inspection. GM has updated VLOM and lifter designs. A DFM disabler (Range Technology) can be used as a preventive measure. Full lifter replacement is rarely needed on C8.
symptoms: Ticking noise from engine on cold start
Tick that goes away when engine warms up
Rough idle briefly on startup
Misfire codes on specific cylinders (rare)

citations.title: YouTube - Engineering Explained: LT2 Engine Valve Lifter Tick and DFM Technology

communityRecommendations.content: TSB 19-NA-218 (revised Dec 2020, covers 2019-2021 C8) is official GM procedure for LT2 lifter tick. Cold-start tick disappearing in 30-60 seconds is normal. Persistent warm tick with rough idle or misfire on cylinders 2, 3, 5, or 8 (DFM deactivation cylinders) indicates collapsed DFM lifter. Have dealer follow full TSB sequence

Range Technology DFM Disabler (RA003B, OBD-II port) is most popular preventive measure to stop DFM cycling. Critical: 2022.5+ C8s require direct-ECU harness plug version, not OBD-II, due to protocol change. For free DFM disabling, Track Mode or Manual Mode in drive mode selector suppresses DFM activation

LT2 DFM deactivates cylinders 2, 3, 5, and 8 - all 8 lifters are collapsible AFM-style and all subject to failure. Driving with collapsed DFM lifter bends pushrod, damages camshaft lobe, and can drop valve debris into cylinder - converting $2,000-3,000 lifter repair into full engine replacement. Do not delay diagnosis on persistent misfire

records.title: Front Trunk (Frunk) Latch and Electrical Issues - C8
records.description: The mid-engine C8 Corvette has reported issues with the front trunk (frunk) latch mechanism. The electronic latch can fail to release or fail to secure properly. GM has issued recalls for frunk latch issues that could allow the frunk to open at speed. Additionally, some C8 owners report various electrical gremlins including infotainment freezes, wireless charging pad failures, and key fob range issues. These are software and build-quality issues typical of a first-generation mid-engine design.
records.solution: Frunk latch: GM recall N212346680 addresses the latch mechanism. Dealer will inspect and replace the latch assembly under recall. Infotainment: ensure software is up to date via dealer or OTA updates. Wireless charger: clean the charging pad and ensure phone case is compatible. Key fob: replace battery (CR2032) and check for interference from aftermarket electronics.
symptoms: Frunk will not open via button or key fob
Frunk opens unexpectedly or does not latch securely
FRUNK AJAR warning when closed properly
Infotainment screen freezing or rebooting
Wireless phone charging pad not working
Key fob range reduced or intermittent

communityRecommendations.content: TSB 21-NA-094 is the key document for inoperative C8 frunk release buttons. Most common cause is water intrusion and corrosion in connector X103 behind front compartment panel (right side). Have dealer inspect X103 for green corrosion - cleaning and re-sealing resolves many failures at zero parts cost

Per TSB 21-NA-094, if X103 is clean, test auxiliary hood latch release switch at connector X102 (access by removing left horn). Switch should read open when not pressed, max 0.2 ohm when pressed. Actual failure is usually internal micro-switch in latch assembly, not mechanical latch. Ensure dealer follows full TSB diagnostic sequence

Do NOT ignore a 'Close Front Trunk' DIC message when frunk IS closed. NHTSA Recall N202311160 was issued for 2020 C8 frunks opening at highway speed. Verify VIN received BCM software update at nhtsa.gov. Persistent false warnings mean latch actuator position sensor has failed - covered under warranty within 3yr/36k miles

records.title: LS7 Valve Guide and Valve Spring Failure - C6 Z06
records.description: The C6 Z06 (2006-2013) uses the LS7 7.0L V8 with titanium intake valves and aggressive valve springs. The exhaust valve guides wear prematurely, allowing valves to cock sideways, break valve springs, and drop valves into cylinders. This is catastrophic engine failure. The issue is most common on 2006-2008 models but can affect all LS7s. GM extended the powertrain warranty but many cars are now beyond coverage. The titanium intake valves and sodium-filled exhaust valves are unique to the LS7.
records.solution: Preventive valve spring and guide replacement is recommended for any LS7 that has not had this service. This requires head removal. Upgraded valve springs from Comp Cams or Manley and bronze valve guides from GM or aftermarket replace the failure-prone components. The LS7 is otherwise an outstanding engine when this issue is addressed.
symptoms: Ticking or clicking noise from engine (valve guide wear)
Misfire on one cylinder (broken spring)
Sudden catastrophic engine failure (dropped valve)
Metal debris in oil
Oil consumption increasing gradually

citations.title: LS7 Valve Drop Issue - Gwatney Performance

communityRecommendations.content: Comp Cams 26918-16 LS7 valve spring kit - upgraded springs that eliminate the failure-prone factory springs
Every LS7 should have valve springs and guides inspected/replaced as preventive maintenance. Budget for this when buying a C6 Z06.
A dropped valve destroys the engine - do NOT wait for symptoms. Preventive spring/guide replacement costs $3k; an engine replacement costs $15k+.

records.title: Bosch ABS/ASR Brake Pressure Modulator Valve (Pump) Failure
records.description: Early C4s (notably 1986-1991) use a Bosch ABS Brake Pressure Modulator Valve (the ABS pump/accumulator assembly); 1990-1991 cars use an updated Bosch system, sometimes with Acceleration Slip Regulation (ASR) traction control. These units fail with age and especially from sitting, and new replacements are effectively unobtainable while good used units are scarce and expensive. Failure typically illuminates the ABS warning lamp and disables anti-lock function (base hydraulic braking is retained).
records.solution: Send the Brake Pressure Modulator Valve to a specialist rebuild/upgrade service that renews the internals to better-than-original spec; this is the accepted fix since new OEM units are gone. Verify wheel-speed sensors and grounds first, as those can mimic modulator faults. Note 1986-1989 and 1990-1991 modules are not interchangeable.
symptoms: ABS warning light on
Anti-lock function inoperative
ABS pump runs excessively or not at all
Brake pedal feel changes with ABS fault

records.title: Brake Pad Hold-Down Spring Breakage
records.description: The hold-down springs that retain the brake pads in the C4's calipers are known to snap in normal use, a problem documented by Haynes and European buyer's guides for the generation. A broken spring lets the pad shift and rattle in the caliper, causing vibration and noise under braking and uneven pad wear. It is cheap to fix but easy to misdiagnose as warped rotors.
records.solution: Replace the broken hardware with the updated stainless-steel hold-down springs (GM part no. 14091366, which fits front or rear calipers), typically done during a routine pad service.
symptoms: Rattle or clunk from a wheel over bumps
Vibration or noise during braking
Squealing or clicking from the caliper
Uneven brake pad wear

records.title: C5 Electronic Steering Column Lock Failure
records.description: Early C5s use an electronic Column Lock mechanism as part of the anti-theft system (fitted to 1997-2004 manual cars and 1997-2000 automatics). The mechanism and its electronics fail with age; when the column fails to unlock at key-on the PCM disables fuel and the car will not drive (or displays 'Service Column Lock'/'Pull Key, Wait Ten Seconds' on the DIC). In some cases the column can lock unexpectedly. It is one of the best-known early-C5 gremlins and is the subject of GM service bulletins and a recall/special policy.
records.solution: Modern accepted fix is to install an electronic column-lock bypass module or the GM relay fix (removes the failure-prone lock function) rather than sourcing the increasingly scarce factory lock assembly. Note on 1997-1998 cars the GM harness/relay is often more BCM-compatible than some aftermarket bypass modules. A BCM reset (pull the relevant fuse ~10 seconds) can temporarily clear the condition.
symptoms: No-crank / no-start or limp (~2 mph) condition
Steering wheel remains locked
'Service Column Lock' / 'Pull Key Wait Ten Seconds' DIC message
Intermittent failure to start
Column unexpectedly locking

records.title: C5 LS1 Harmonic Balancer (Crank Pulley) Separation
records.description: The LS1's press-on harmonic balancer uses a rubber isolator ring between the hub and outer pulley. With age and heat the rubber separates, letting the outer ring wobble and slip. Early symptom is a faint chirp at idle before a visible wobble develops. If ignored the balancer can walk forward on the crank snout, throw the serpentine belt, damage accessories, and in severe cases contribute to crankshaft damage. Enthusiasts note the degradation is time-driven, not just mileage-driven.
records.solution: Replace the harmonic balancer. Because installation requires pressing the balancer fully onto the crank snout with the correct tool (and the tight C5 nose often requires removing the steering rack/lowering the cradle), many owners upgrade to a bolt-together aftermarket unit (e.g., ATI Super Damper or PowerBond) rather than reinstalling the stock press-fit style. Inspect crank snout and keyway during the job.
symptoms: Visible wobble of crank pulley at idle
Chirping or squealing at idle
Belt misalignment or thrown serpentine belt
Vibration
Erratic accessory operation

records.title: Cooling Fan Relay Failure and Late Fan Engagement (Overheating)
records.description: C4 cooling fans are relay-controlled and factory-programmed to switch on at very high coolant temperatures (around 230-238°F, set for emissions compliance), so any weakness in the fan relay or coolant temperature sensor quickly tips the car into overheating in traffic. Fan relays are a recognized common failure on these cars, and on 1992-1996 LT1 models the fan circuit is also routed through the HVAC refrigerant pressure switch, so a discharged A/C system can keep the fans from running. Chronic overheating risks head gasket damage and accelerates Opti-Spark failure on LT1 cars.
records.solution: Test and replace the failed cooling fan relay and/or coolant temperature sensor — both are inexpensive parts. Many owners also install an earlier fan turn-on switch or adjust fan programming (roughly 200-210°F) and keep the A/C system charged on LT1 cars so the fan circuit operates normally.
symptoms: Temperature gauge climbing in traffic or at idle
Cooling fan never audibly kicks on
Fans only run when the A/C is on
Coolant boiling over or overflow tank venting
Overheating that disappears at highway speed

records.title: Cross-Fire Injection Driveability Problems (1984 L83)
records.description: The 1984-only L83 Cross-Fire engine uses twin throttle-body injectors managed by an early ECM with a single O2 sensor and one idle-air control circuit for two IAC valves, so the two throttle bodies easily fall out of sync. Throttle shafts ride directly in the soft aluminum housings and wear, intake manifolds leak, and the system is highly sensitive to a failing coolant temperature sensor and oil pressure switch. Owners see surging or rough idle, hesitation, stalling once warmed up, and rich running that modern shops often struggle to diagnose.
records.solution: Restore the system to spec: replace the coolant temperature sensor (updated weather-pack type) and oil pressure switch, reseal the intake manifold, rebuild or rebush worn throttle bodies, clean or replace injectors, and synchronize the two throttle bodies. Specialist Cross-Fire shops can rebuild the throttle bodies when wear is advanced.
symptoms: Surging or hunting idle
Engine stalls or dies once at operating temperature
Hesitation or stumble on acceleration
Runs rich with poor fuel economy
Hard starting when warm

records.title: Digital LCD Instrument Cluster Failure (1984-1989)
records.description: The 1984-1989 C4's all-digital LCD dash is a notorious failure point now that the electronics are decades old. Heat and vibration crack solder joints on the backlight board connectors and internal power supply, electrolytic capacitors age out, sunlight fades the LCD polarizing film, and the photocell dimmer degrades. The result is a cluster that goes dark, flickers random segments, or becomes unreadable in daylight, leaving the driver without speed, fuel, or temperature information.
records.solution: Rebuild the cluster: re-solder or replace the backlight connectors and power supply components, replace the polarizing film and photocell, and install fresh bulbs. DIY component kits run under $100, while professional cluster rebuilding services handle the complete job.
symptoms: Cluster completely dark with ignition on
Backlighting very dim, too bright, or intermittent
Randomly flickering LCD segments
Display faded and only readable with polarized sunglasses or a flashlight
Cluster stuck dim due to a bad photocell
Cruise control won't set

records.title: Digital LCD Instrument Cluster Scrambling / Backlight Failure
records.description: The 1990-1996 C4 dash uses analog sweep gauges with a central digital LCD readout (the 1984-1989 cars were fully digital). With age the LCD can scramble into an unreadable mess, especially when the car hits bumps, which is characteristic of a ground/connection problem. Segments drop out, the display flickers, backlight bulbs fail, and the fuel-gauge/'FUEL RATE' readings become erratic. Heat, vibration, aged solder joints, and a degraded polarizer film are the root causes.
records.solution: Send the cluster to a specialist rebuild service (re-solders connections, replaces backlight bulbs, and renews the polarized LCD film), or DIY the polarizer film replacement and re-solder cold joints. For fuel-gauge creep and wrong FUEL RATE readings, repair the ground wire at the center lock pillar on coupes. Cleaning/re-seating cluster ground connections often resolves bump-induced scrambling.
symptoms: Scrambled/unreadable LCD, especially over bumps
Dim or dead backlighting
Flickering display
Missing LCD segments
Fuel gauge creeping / wrong FUEL RATE reading
Blurry display film

records.title: Electronic Column Lock (ECL) Failure - NHTSA Recall 04V060
records.description: The electronic column lock system on 1997-2004 C5 Corvettes can fail to unlock when the vehicle is started, leaving the steering wheel locked. The car is designed to shut off fuel above 2 mph if the column stays locked, but if PCM voltage drops the fuel shutoff may not engage and the vehicle can be accelerated while unsteerable. A 'Service Column Lock' or 'Pull Key and Wait 10 Seconds' message often appears on the DIC. GM Recall 04006 (NHTSA 04V060000) covered ~126,624 vehicles; on automatics the lock plate is removed, on manuals the PCM is reflashed and lock plate inspected/replaced. Despite the recall, thousands of owners still report the warning afterward.
records.solution: Verify recall 04006 (NHTSA 04V060000) has been performed - dealers handle free of charge. On automatics the lock plate is physically removed; on manuals the PCM is reprogrammed and lock plate inspected. Aftermarket bypass kits (relay between BCM and lock motor) are available for cars still throwing the message post-recall. Keep battery voltage healthy - low voltage at the PCM is the trigger.
symptoms: 'Service Column Lock' message on DIC
'Pull Key and Wait 10 Seconds' warning
Steering wheel will not unlock after starting
Engine cranks but vehicle limited to 2 mph
Intermittent column lock activation while driving

records.title: Fuel Level Sending Unit Failure / Erratic Gas Gauge
records.description: C4 fuel level sending units are a long-standing failure item: corrosion forms where the resistive winding is grounded through a spring, the wiper develops open spots, or the float hangs up against the tank's inner wall. The gauge then sticks on full or empty, jumps erratically, or throws off the trip computer's range display. Owners can unexpectedly run out of fuel, which also risks overheating the in-tank electric fuel pump.
records.solution: Drop the tank or access the sender, then clean the resistive winding and ground contact or replace the sending unit outright — most shops replace the in-tank fuel pump and strainer at the same time since the labor overlaps. New sending units alone run $300 or more.
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck on full regardless of fuel level
Gauge stuck on empty or reading erratically
Fuel reading jumps while driving
Trip computer range/fuel data inaccurate
Running out of gas with the gauge showing fuel remaining

records.title: LS1 Excessive Oil Consumption (PCV System and Ring Pack)
records.description: 1997-2002 C5 Corvettes with the LS1 (and 2001-2004 Z06 with LS6) can consume oil at rates of 1 quart per 2,000-3,500 miles or worse. Root causes are blow-by from poor cylinder bore tolerances paired with thin, flat-faced piston rings, exacerbated by a marginal factory PCV system that pools oil in the hoses and pulls it into the intake. The problem hits manual-transmission cars driven hard above 3,200 RPM hardest. GM issued service bulletins acknowledging 'higher than expected oil consumption' on 1999-2002 Corvettes. The LS6 valley cover with its integrated PCV baffle can also seal poorly, sending oil directly into the intake.
records.solution: Install an oil catch can in the PCV return line - many owners report consumption drops from 1 qt/3,500 miles to 1-2 ounces per oil change. Upgrade to LS6-style PCV plumbing on LS1 cars. For LS6, verify valley cover PCV baffle is properly sealed. Use GM-spec 5W-30 (do not run thicker - the LS rings are designed for it). If consumption exceeds 1 qt/1,000 miles, a ring/cylinder reseal is the only permanent fix.
symptoms: Oil consumption 1 quart per 2,000-3,500 miles
Oil pooled in PCV hoses on inspection
Carbon buildup on intake valves
Oil residue at throttle body
Worse with frequent operation above 3,200 RPM

records.title: Opti-Spark (Optispark) Distributor Failure on LT1/LT4 Engines
records.description: The LT1 (and 1996 LT4) uses a front-of-engine 'Opti-Spark' optical distributor mounted low behind the water pump, driven off the camshaft. It is highly vulnerable to moisture, heat, and ozone. The 1992-1993 units were completely unvented and are notorious for internal condensation and corrosion of the optical sensor disc. The leading real-world cause of failure is a leaking water pump directly above it dripping coolant onto/into the unit, but ordinary humidity and age also kill them. It is one of the single most defining reliability weak points of the 1992-1996 C4.
records.solution: Replace the Opti-Spark distributor (later vented-style unit is the upgrade for 92-93 cars; a vacuum-vented design arrived on 1995-1996 units). Because the water pump sits directly above it and is the most common contaminant source, the accepted practice is to replace the water pump at the same time ('while you're in there'), since the front cover/serpentine and much labor overlaps. Many owners also drill/tap the water pump weep hole and route a hose away from the distributor.
symptoms: Intermittent misfire
Rough running / stumbling
Stalling
No-start (especially after rain or high humidity)
Misfire that worsens when engine/weather is damp
Backfiring

records.title: Opti-Spark Optical Distributor Failure (LT1)
records.description: The 1992-1996 LT1 uses the Opti-Spark optical distributor mounted low on the front of the engine, directly behind the water pump. Undersized factory vent/drain holes trap condensation, and any coolant seepage from the water pump weep hole or oil from the front crank seal corrodes the optical sensor and internal contacts. When the high-resolution signal degrades, the engine misfires, backfires, and can stall without warning and refuse to restart, often stranding the owner. The 1995-1996 vented design lasts longer but still fails with age.
records.solution: Replace the distributor with a vented (1995-96 style) or upgraded aftermarket Opti-Spark, and replace the water pump at the same time since pump leaks are a primary killer of the new unit. Labor is significant (roughly 4-7 hours) because the water pump, balancer, and accessories must come off; some owners convert to aftermarket coil-pack ignition.
symptoms: Misfire or skip that worsens at higher RPM
Backfiring through the intake or exhaust
Stumbling or stalling in damp weather or after washing the engine
Extended cranking or no-start
Engine suddenly dies while driving and won't restart
Rough idle

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump / Fuel Sending Unit Failure
records.description: Essentially every 1984-1996 C4 eventually needs its in-tank electric fuel pump. A high-pitched whine from behind the seats is the classic early warning. In-tank connectors become brittle and corroded (adding resistance and overworking the new pump), and the fuel-level sending unit float/rheostat fails, giving inaccurate fuel readings. Ethanol-blend fuels sitting in these older systems accelerate the damage; the original strainer 'sock' also clogs with age.
records.solution: Replace the fuel pump together with the fuel strainer/sock and inspect/replace the in-tank wiring connectors; replace the fuel-level sending unit if gauge readings are off. On C4s this requires dropping/removing the tank. Use fresh fuel and avoid long-term ethanol storage.
symptoms: High-pitched whine from behind seats
Hard starting or extended cranking
No-start / no fuel pressure
Stalling under load
Inaccurate or erratic fuel gauge

records.title: Targa Top and Weatherstrip Water Leaks
records.description: C4 weatherstrip rubber hardens, shrinks, and cracks with age and UV exposure, and the removable targa roof panel relies entirely on these seals. Leaks are most common at the front corners where the windshield A-pillar, targa panel, and door glass meet, and at the lower corners of the rear hatch on coupes. The result is water dripping into the cabin, soaked carpet (which can damage electronics and breed mildew), wind noise, and drafts; a poorly adjusted top or cheap aftermarket rubber makes it worse.
records.solution: Replace the aged weatherstrip with quality seals as a complete kit, adjust the targa top latch/fit per the factory procedure, and maintain the new rubber with weatherstrip lubricant. It is a manageable DIY weekend job; shops charge more for a full reseal.
symptoms: Water dripping at the windshield corner or targa edge in rain or car wash
Wet carpet or damp smell in the cabin
Wind noise at speed around the roof panel or doors
Visibly cracked, hardened, or flattened door/roof seals
Drafts around the targa panel

records.title: Water Pump Front Seal Leak (Damages Opti-Spark)
records.description: The LT1/LT4 mechanical water pump develops a front seal failure with age, allowing coolant to pass into a chamber that has no outlet except the bottom weep hole. Because the water pump sits directly above the Opti-Spark distributor, the dripping coolant frequently contaminates and destroys the distributor, turning a routine water pump job into a much larger repair. Coolant seeping from the weep hole is the classic warning sign.
records.solution: Replace the water pump when weeping is observed; do not defer, given the Opti-Spark below it. Standard practice is to replace the Opti-Spark at the same time if any contamination has occurred, or proactively since the labor overlaps. Owners commonly drill/tap the weep hole and route clear hose away from the distributor to protect it from any future seepage.
symptoms: Coolant drip/stain from weep hole under front of engine
Low coolant level
Overheating
Sweet coolant smell
Subsequent Opti-Spark misfire/no-start

records.title: ZR-1 LT5 Fuel Injector (Multec) Failure
records.description: The ZR-1's DOHC LT5 uses 16 fuel injectors (primary and secondary sets), and the original Rochester Multec units from this era are known to fail — coil windings short and drop resistance, and the early 1990-1992 injectors were designed before widespread ethanol-blended fuel, which degrades them further. Because the engine runs mostly on its primary injectors, failures show up as rough idle, stumbling, and misfires that integrate-port diagnosis often traces to multiple dead or leaking injectors. Replacement is costly since the plenum must come off and ZR-1 specialists commonly find several failed injectors at once.
records.solution: Remove the plenum and replace or have all 16 injectors professionally refurbished with modern ethanol-resistant equivalents; ZR-1 specialists recommend doing the full set plus seals while the plenum is off rather than chasing individual failures.
symptoms: Rough or lumpy idle
Stumble or hesitation on acceleration
Misfire on specific cylinders
Check engine light with O2 sensor reading high or low
Fuel smell or fuel-diluted oil from a leaking injector
Knocking noise from the dual-mass flywheel under uneven running

records.title: Driveline Vibration at Low Speed - C7
records.description: The C7 Corvette with the 7-speed manual or 8-speed automatic can develop an annoying driveline vibration/shudder at low speeds, particularly during gentle acceleration from a stop. The 7-speed manual uses a dual-mass flywheel that can develop chatter. The 8-speed automatic (8L90) shares the torque converter shudder issue with GM trucks. The transaxle-mounted differential and half-shafts can also contribute to vibrations.
records.solution: For 8-speed: same transmission fluid exchange with Mobil 1 LV ATF HP as other 8L90 vehicles. For 7-speed manual: dual-mass flywheel inspection/replacement, or conversion to single-mass flywheel with aftermarket clutch. Half-shaft inspection for worn CV joints. Some vibration at low speed is inherent to the C7 design.
symptoms: Shudder during gentle acceleration from stop
Vibration at 20-40 mph under light throttle (8-speed)
Clutch chatter in 1st gear (7-speed manual)
Vibration through floor at highway cruise
Clunk on tip-in/tip-out throttle

records.title: Steering Column Lock (VATS) Failure - Cannot Start
records.description: The C5 Corvette has a notorious electronic steering column lock (part of the Vehicle Anti-Theft System / VATS) that fails, preventing the car from starting. When the column lock module fails, the car displays "SERVICE COLUMN LOCK" and refuses to start even with the correct key. The column lock motor or position sensor fails, and GM designed it as a security feature that defaults to locked when it fails. This can strand you anywhere. It is the #1 most-discussed C5 reliability issue.
records.solution: The permanent fix is to bypass or disable the column lock. Delphi (OEM supplier) sells a bypass module that plugs into the column lock connector and eliminates the lock function while keeping the anti-theft system working. Many C5 owners bypass the column lock preemptively before it fails. GM dealers can also reprogram the BCM to disable the column lock. A failed column lock module can be replaced but the new one will eventually fail too.
symptoms: SERVICE COLUMN LOCK message on DIC
Car will not start - ignition will not turn
Intermittent no-start that resolves by waiting
Steering wheel locked and cannot be turned
Key fob works but ignition does not

citations.title: NHTSA Vehicle Page for 1997 Chevrolet Corvette - Includes complaints related to steering column lock and VATS issues
YouTube - ChrisFix: How to Fix a Steering Column Lock on a Chevrolet Corvette

communityRecommendations.content: Bypass the column lock preemptively before it fails and strands you. CorvetteForum.com has detailed DIY bypass guides. The bypass is a simple wiring modification.
If stranded with SERVICE COLUMN LOCK, try turning the key to ON (not start) and waiting 10-15 minutes. Sometimes the lock resets.
If buying a used C5, ask if the column lock has been bypassed. If not, plan to do it immediately - failure is a matter of when, not if.

records.title: Dry Sump Oil System Issues - C6 Z06/ZR1
records.description: The C6 Z06 (LS7) and ZR1 (LS9) use a dry sump oil system with an external oil tank and scavenge pump. The oil tank can develop internal baffle failure, and the scavenge pump lines can leak at fittings. The dry sump system is more complex than the wet sump in base C6 models. Oil level must be checked differently (engine must be running to get accurate level). Overfilling or underfilling can cause issues. Some owners report oil starvation during sustained high-G cornering despite the dry sump design.
records.solution: Inspect dry sump lines and fittings for leaks. Check oil level with engine running at operating temperature. Use the correct GM Mobil 1 5W-30 oil and do not overfill. For track use, an oil cooler upgrade and LG Motorsports or similar dry sump upgrade improve oil control under sustained G-loads.
symptoms: Low oil pressure warning during hard cornering
Oil leak from dry sump lines or fittings
Oil level difficult to read accurately
Oil foaming (overfilled or air ingestion)
Scavenge pump noise

records.title: Harmonic Balancer Failure - C5 LS1/LS6
records.description: The C5 Corvette LS1 and LS6 engines have a known harmonic balancer (crankshaft pulley) failure. The rubber bonding between the inner hub and outer ring separates, causing the outer ring to wobble or walk off the crankshaft. This can destroy the serpentine belt, damage the timing cover, and in severe cases score the crankshaft snout. The issue typically occurs between 80,000-150,000 miles. A wobbling harmonic balancer also throws off ignition timing and can cause engine damage.
records.solution: Replace the harmonic balancer. ATI Super Damper is the definitive upgrade - it uses elastomer O-rings instead of bonded rubber, making it essentially lifetime. The GM replacement balancer will eventually fail the same way. Installation requires a balancer puller and installer tool. While the balancer is off, replace the front crank seal.
symptoms: Wobbling or vibrating crankshaft pulley (visible)
Serpentine belt walking off pulleys or shredding
Knocking or rattling noise from front of engine
Check engine light with misfire codes
Oil leak from front crank seal (balancer walks off)
AC/PS failure from broken belt

citations.title: NHTSA Complaint #10451750 - 2001 Chevrolet Corvette crank pulley / harmonic balancer failure
